fatality_rate.notes: Symptomatic case-fatality rate for seasonal influenza is low and varies substantially by season severity and age group. Mortality is heavily concentrated in adults 65+ (about two-thirds of deaths in recent U.S. seasons) and is far lower in children and young adults. The typical value (0.07%) reflects symptomatic-case denominators for seasonal influenza. Case definition drives fatality rate estimates by orders of magnitude: a systematic review of the 2009 H1N1 pandemic found estimates ranging from ~0.001-0.01% using an infections denominator, ~0-1.2% using a symptomatic-cases denominator, and ~0-13.5% using a laboratory-confirmed-cases denominator, with the latter most prone to ascertainment bias since testing is typically reserved for more severe presentations. Any fatality rate figure should be interpreted alongside its denominator definition.

fatality_rate.notes: Fatality is high without treatment (historically ~50-80%) but drops sharply with prompt antibiotic therapy to roughly 10-15% overall. U.S. age-stratified data (1998-2007) shows a clear age gradient even among treated cases: 6% in infants <1 year, 9.7% in adolescents 14-17, and 13.6% in young adults 18-24 — the opposite pattern from raw incidence, which is highest in infants. Recent surveillance also found an unusually high 18% fatality rate for an emerging serogroup Y strain (2023-2024), compared to 11% in the preceding 2017-2021 period.

immunity_duration.notes: Natural immunity is continuously reinforced by intermittent carriage rather than following a single post-infection decay curve (see estimates below). Vaccine-induced immunity duration differs by vaccine type: CDC's booster schedule implies MenACWY protection lasts roughly 4-5 years before meaningful waning (booster at 16 after initial dose at 11-12; every-5-year boosters for ongoing high risk), while MenB protection appears shorter-lived, with boosters recommended as early as 1-3 years post-series, or within 6-12 months during active outbreaks. Antibody-persistence cohort studies (Zangwill et al.) found vaccine-induced bactericidal activity detectable up to 10 years post-vaccination, though substantially declined by year 2.

r0.notes: Estimates vary enormously by transmission setting rather than clustering around one 'general population' value, since most HAV transmission is fecal-oral/foodborne rather than driven by the direct-contact networks these R0 estimates characterize. Close-contact/direct-transmission outbreaks among naive children (e.g., schools) show R0 of 1.9-2.5; modeling of sexual/close-contact transmission in high-risk adult populations (MSM) spans 1.71-3.67. People who inject drugs (PWID) — a leading driver of recent U.S. person-to-person HAV outbreaks — show the widest and often highest state-level estimates (2.2-5.0 across 16 US states), with a pooled herd immunity threshold of 64% (90% prediction interval: 52-76%), reflecting dense, frequent direct-contact/sharing networks.

estimate_extremes.title: Ebola disease
Ebola haemorrhagic fever in Zaire, 1976

fatality_rate.notes: WHO estimate. Among the highest CFRs of any human pathogen, but the range is enormous and driven more by care setting and species than by anything intrinsic to a given outbreak. Species ordering is consistent: Zaire ebolavirus is the most lethal (roughly 60-90% historically), Sudan ebolavirus intermediate (roughly 40-60%), Bundibugyo ebolavirus lowest (roughly 25-40%). Reston ebolavirus has caused no known human illness. Supportive care matters enormously — aggressive fluid and electrolyte management alone cut mortality substantially in the 2014-2016 epidemic, and the monoclonal antibody therapeutics (mAb114 / ansuvimab and REGN-EB3 / inmazeb) proven in the 2018-2020 DRC PALM trial reduced mortality to roughly 30% overall and into the single digits among patients treated early with low viral load. Reported outbreak CFRs are also inflated or deflated by outcome ascertainment: cases lost to follow-up are disproportionately survivors in some datasets and disproportionately deaths in others.

average_contacts_daily.notes: Not meaningfully captured by a general daily-contacts metric. Transmission requires direct contact with blood, vomit, stool, or other body fluids from a symptomatic patient or a corpse, so conversational-contact surveys such as POLYMOD are a poor proxy — the relevant exposure set is caregivers, burial participants, and unprotected health workers, not the general contact network. The usual substitutes in the literature are household secondary attack rate (pooled at roughly 12-17%, rising sharply with the intimacy of care provided) and funeral attendance, and transmission is strongly overdispersed at the individual level. If a contact-network model is required, parameterize on household and care-contact structure plus discrete funeral events rather than on a mean daily contact count.

estimate_extremes.title: Long-term cellular immunity of vaccines for Zaire Ebola Virus Diseases
Ebola virus disease

immunity_duration.notes: This field pools two quantities that should not be averaged: immunity after natural infection and immunity after vaccination. The estimates below are also all immunological markers, not protection — no correlate of protection has been established for EVD, challenge studies are impossible, and reinfection exposure is too rare to measure protection directly, so every value here is a floor on detectable immune memory rather than a duration of immunity. Natural infection: IgG and some neutralizing activity persisted in all 14 Yambuku survivors tested 40 years on, and no well-documented same-species reinfection has been reported, but tertiary sources split between 'lifelong' (ECDC) and '10 years or more' (Penn Medicine); the conservative reading is a 10-year floor with lifelong as an upper assumption, not two compatible claims. Vaccine: PREVAC found EBOV-specific memory T-cell responses at 60 months with no decline, but only after 8-day in-vitro expansion — ex-vivo responses were undetectable by month 12 and antibody titres had fallen to near pre-boost levels by then, so recall capacity persists while circulating effector immunity does not. No booster schedule is defined and no immunological criterion for revaccination exists. Cross-protection between species should not be assumed: Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) targets Zaire ebolavirus only and offers no reliable protection against Sudan ebolavirus, which is why the 2022 Uganda Sudan-virus outbreak had no licensed vaccine. For modeling, prefer the 3650-day floor for recovered individuals, treat vaccine-derived immunity as a separate compartment with a waning rate the data cannot currently pin down, and run sensitivity analysis rather than committing to a point value.
immunity_duration.special_value: lifelong; natural infection: at least 10 years, plausibly lifelong; vaccine: memory demonstrated to 5 years, protection duration unknown

estimate_extremes.title: Transmissibility and Pathogenicity of Ebola Virus: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Household Secondary Attack Rate and Asymptomatic Infection
Impact of asymptomatic infection and acquired immunity on the spread and control of Ebola

asymptomatic_fraction.notes: The single most contested parameter for this pathogen, with credible published estimates spanning more than an order of magnitude. The disagreement is largely methodological: seroprevalence studies in contacts pick up antibody-positive people who never reported illness, but Ebola serological assays have known specificity problems in populations with high background reactivity, and recall of mild illness months after an epidemic is poor. Studies using stricter case definitions and better-validated assays tend to land far lower than the early Gabon work. Consequential modeling caveat: asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic individuals are not believed to transmit, since infectiousness tracks viral load and symptom severity — so unlike most respiratory pathogens, a high asymptomatic fraction here reduces the susceptible pool without adding hidden transmission chains. Setting this parameter high therefore makes outbreaks easier to control in most model structures, which is the opposite of the usual intuition and worth checking explicitly in sensitivity analysis.

r0.note: Typical value taken from mean of systematic review of multiple countries with over 2000 studies reviewed.

fatality_rate.review_note: Maximum of 25% comes from a case series of patients in an ICU, not a population case fatality; the other estimates (0.05% to 0.07%) are surveillance figures. Needs the ICU estimate scoped to the population it describes, or left out of the range.

average_contacts_daily.notes: STRUCTURALLY INAPPLICABLE, not merely unmeasured: dengue has no human-to-human contact route, so any value here would be actively misleading rather than uncertain, and no default should be imputed. The transmission-relevant analogues are vector-to-human ratio, per-mosquito daily biting rate and per-bite transmission probabilities, which combine into vectorial capacity and belong in their own parameter block.

estimate_extremes.title: Interactions between serotypes of dengue highlight epidemiological impact of cross-immunity

immunity_duration.notes: DO NOT COLLAPSE TO A SINGLE WANING RATE: homotypic immunity is effectively lifelong while heterotypic cross-protection lasts roughly 1-3 years, and waning does not return people to baseline susceptibility but to an antibody-dependent-enhancement state with higher severe-disease risk. Vaccine-derived immunity is a further separate compartment that must be stratified by baseline serostatus and serotype, never pooled with natural infection.
immunity_duration.special_value: lifelong; homotypic (same serotype): lifelong; heterotypic cross-protection: roughly 1-3 years, then reversion to susceptibility WITH ENHANCED SEVERITY RISK

r0.notes: MODEL STRUCTURE DOMINATES SETTING: fitted to the same series, SIRS structures give 1-2 while structures with gradual acquisition of partial immunity give 5-7, so an RSV R0 is uninterpretable without the assumed immunity structure. Because RSV is endemic and almost nobody is fully susceptible after infancy, most published values are effective rather than basic reproduction numbers, and values below unity in the estimates reflect partial population immunity rather than a non-viable pathogen.

estimate_extremes.title: Respiratory syncytial virus

infectious_days.notes: STRONGLY AGE-STRATIFIED, and this is the dominant source of spread rather than measurement error: shedding runs about 18 days in infants against 9 days in adults, and 13.5 days in symptomatic against 7.8 in asymptomatic episodes. Sampling intensity and detection method also drive the estimate — infrequent symptom-triggered sampling and culture give short durations, frequent PCR surveillance gives long ones — so a single scalar here will misrepresent whichever age group the model cares about.
infectious_days.review_note: Typical 11.2 days has no citation and looks like a PCR shedding duration; both cited estimates give 6.5 days (range 4 to 10). Needs a transmission window with a citation, or the shedding figure scoped as shedding.

estimate_extremes.population: US infants and children under 5 with RSV
estimate_extremes.title: Mortality Among US Infants and Children Under 5 Years of Age with Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Bronchiolitis: A Systematic Literature Review

fatality_rate.notes: DENOMINATOR AND AGE BOTH DECIDE THIS: deaths per LRTI episode in under-5s is about 0.31%. Mortality is concentrated at the two ends of life — infants under 6 months account for roughly 46% of paediatric RSV deaths, and 97% of those deaths occur in LMICs — so an age-flat fatality rate is the single worst simplification available for this pathogen.
fatality_rate.review_note: Typical 0.31% is deaths per lower-respiratory-infection episode in children under 5, and the 1.7% maximum is an inpatient case fatality; the simulation counts every infection as a case, so either would overstate deaths. Needs a fatality per infection, or the estimates scoped to the population and denominator they describe.

average_contacts_daily.notes: No validateable information found for RSV daily contacts.

estimate_extremes.title: Kinetics of the Neutralizing Antibody Response to Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections in a Birth Cohort
Respiratory Syncytial Virus Reinfections in Children in Western Australia

immunity_duration.notes: The typical value is based on the third estimate. SHORT, PARTIAL AND NEVER STERILIZING — reinfection throughout life is the norm for RSV, including within a single season, and repeat infection does not require antigenic change. Immunity attenuates severity more than it prevents infection, so the correct model structure returns people to a reduced-severity susceptible state rather than holding them in a recovered compartment; no correlate of protection is established, so every value here is an interval between detected infections rather than a measured protection duration.

asymptomatic_fraction.notes: The typical is based on the first estimate as it includes all ages, urban and rural household cohort. Driven by age and by surveillance intensity rather than by genuine disagreement: infants are the most symptomatic group and give the lowest fractions, while cohorts sampling on a fixed schedule regardless of symptoms find far more silent infection than clinic-based or symptom-triggered designs. Detection method compounds this, since serology-only ascertainment counts both truly silent infection and illness the surveillance missed, so the definition of asymptomatic should be recorded alongside any value used.
